title: Session security deep analysis: session fixation, token entropy, cookie flags, and session invalidation after logout
goal: WebGoat has hijacksession and spoofcookie modules. ZAP passive scan catches some cookie flags but misses session-layer attacks. Implement a session-security runner: (1) Session Fixation: check if the application issues a new session token after login. If the pre-login session ID remains valid post-authentication → session fixation vulnerability. (2) Cookie Security Flags: for every Set-Cookie header, verify: Secure flag present, HttpOnly flag present, SameSite=Strict or Lax, not exposed over HTTP. Missing any of these → Medium finding per missing flag. (3) Session Token Entropy: collect 10 consecutive session tokens and test for: sequential/predictable patterns, length < 128 bits, character set too small. Low entropy → High finding. (4) Session Invalidation: after logout, replay the captured session token. If server still accepts it → session not properly invalidated. Finding: 'Session Not Invalidated on Logout — allows session replay attacks'. (5) Concurrent Session Limits: login from two sessions simultaneously; check if both work (some apps should limit concurrent sessions). (6) Session Token in URL: check if session IDs appear in URL parameters (visible in referrer headers and access logs). All active tier. Findings include severity Medium-High.
scope: WebGoat hijacksession + spoofcookie modules. Current coverage ⚠️ (partial — ZAP catches some cookie flags passively). Full session security requires active probing not possible with passive scan alone.
generation_reason: Session fixation, token entropy, and post-logout replay are not currently tested — WebGoat has dedicated modules, Burp Suite tests these via session handling rules.
